concepts.title: Concept of Business: Economic Activity with Profit Motive

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Concept of Business: Economic Activity with Profit Motive' refers to.
questions.a: Business is an economic activity involving the production or purchase and sale of goods and services with the objective of earning profit by satisfying human needs in society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Concept of Business: Economic Activity with Profit Motive'.
questions.a: Business undertakings deal in goods and services on a regular basis, bear risk and uncertainty, and reward the entrepreneur with profit for bearing it.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Concept of Business: Economic Activity with Profit Motive' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Industry and Its Types: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Industry and Its Types: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary' refers to.
questions.a: Industry refers to economic activities that convert resources into useful goods, grouped as primary industries extracting nature's products, secondary industries manufacturing and construction, and tertiary industries providing support services.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Industry and Its Types: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary'.
questions.a: Genetic industries like poultry and mining extractive work sit beside manufacturing industries that process materials into finished goods.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Industry and Its Types: Primary, Secondary and Tertiary' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Commerce: Trade and Aids to Trade

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Commerce: Trade and Aids to Trade' refers to.
questions.a: Commerce includes all activities that remove the hindrances of person, place, time, risk, finance and knowledge between producers and consumers, and it has two branches, namely trade and aids to trade.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Commerce: Trade and Aids to Trade'.
questions.a: Trade is the buying and selling of goods, while banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, advertising and communication act as aids to trade.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Commerce: Trade and Aids to Trade' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Business Risk: Nature and Causes' refers to.
questions.a: Business risk refers to the possibility of inadequate profits or losses because of uncertainties or unexpected events, and it arises from natural, human, economic and other causes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Business Risk: Nature and Causes'.
questions.a: Risk is an essential part of business, its degree depends on the scale of operations, and profit is the reward for taking risk.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Business Risk: Nature and Causes' taught, and from which source text?
